description: Node 3 — Insurance Risk Translation Room. Insurance / reinsurance / financial-lines specialists translate the Node 1+2 behavioral risk findings (and the realized litigation/settlement/2025-ruling) into D&O/E&O underwriting variables, claims triggers, litigation-tail reserving, reinsurance accumulation, and the AI-agent-liability analogy.
setting: A post-event insurance war-game: financial-lines / D&O / E&O / reinsurance / claims / emerging-risk / AI-risk specialists convene to convert the Credit Suisse crisis and its creditor-litigation aftermath into concrete, usable insurance risk variables and a loss-propagation map.

agents.persona_description: Prices and underwrites the financial-lines book. Wants priceable, containable exposure; skeptical of overstated severity; tightens terms, pricing and warranties.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Translate exposure into pricing, terms, exclusions and governance warranties
behavioral_tendencies.decision_bias: Keeps the book priceable and contained

levers: tighten policy terms and add exclusions/sublimits
reprice the financial-lines book to the loss experience
demand governance warranties and risk-control evidence

initial_knowledge.content: The Credit Suisse losses drove rising D&O premiums, stricter underwriting, and governance-linked coverage terms across the bank D&O market.
A $115M D&O settlement (19 CS directors/officers, risk-management failures) is a concrete severity benchmark, paid by the D&O insurers.

agents.persona_description: Maps directors-and-officers liability exposure: the securities suits, the settlement, and the governance red flags that trigger D&O claims.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Surface D&O claim triggers and severity from the governance failures

levers: map director/officer claim triggers (misrepresentation of controls)
cite the securities class actions and the $115M settlement
tie governance red flags to D&O loss

initial_knowledge.content: A March 2023 securities class action named Credit Suisse and its officers (Chairman Lehmann, CEO Korner) over non-disclosure of deposit outflows and 'material weaknesses' in internal controls — the canonical D&O trigger.
19 CS directors/officers settled for $115M (risk-management failures incl. Archegos $5.5bn), paid by the D&O insurers; multi-year tail (2020-21 conduct to 2025).
The Swiss PUK found years of board/exec mismanagement (CHF 11bn fines, CHF 32.3bn losses) and FINMA's 2017 'regulatory filter' that overstated equity by ~CHF 15.3bn.

agents.persona_description: Assesses errors-and-omissions / professional-liability exposure for advisers and auditors implicated in the failure.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Surface E&O exposure for auditors and professional advisers
behavioral_tendencies.stress_response: Widens the net of implicated professionals

levers: flag auditor (KPMG/PwC) and adviser E&O exposure
tie standard-of-care breaches to claims
map professional-liability triggers

initial_knowledge.content: The PUK and FAOA flagged deficiencies in KPMG's CS audits (2015/2018/2019) and PwC's (2022) — professional-liability exposure for the auditors.

agents.persona_description: Assesses accumulation across the reinsurance portfolio — correlated D&O/E&O losses from one systemic event, and AI-correlation accumulation.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Model treaty accumulation and correlated catastrophe exposure

levers: flag correlated D&O across SVB/Signature/CS from one event
model treaty accumulation and clash
identify hidden AI-correlation accumulation

initial_knowledge.content: The Archegos failure hit Nomura, Goldman, UBS and Morgan Stanley simultaneously; clustered securities suits across SVB/Signature/CS — one systemic event correlates D&O/E&O losses across insureds and treaties.
Lloyd's warns firms separately using LLMs for underwriting can 'inadvertently correlate themselves' via shared training data — hidden, hard-to-discover reinsurance accumulation.

agents.persona_description: Reserves for the multi-year litigation tail: the AT1 bondholder suits and the 2025 court ruling that the write-off was unlawful.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Reserve for the litigation tail and assess recovery/duration

levers: reserve for the multi-year AT1 litigation
cite the 2025 Swiss Federal Administrative Court 'unlawful' ruling
model recovery uncertainty and a ~6-year horizon

initial_knowledge.content: Quinn Emanuel leads multi-jurisdiction AT1 bondholder litigation (~CHF 16.5bn / $17bn); a 2024 SDNY suit sued Switzerland on an expropriation theory.

On 14 Oct 2025 the Swiss Federal Administrative Court ruled FINMA's write-off UNLAWFUL (no legal basis; viability event not triggered; Art. 5a Emergency Ordinance unconstitutional); ~3,000 complainants; forecast up to ~6 years; appealable.

agents.persona_description: Assesses reputational contagion and systemic emerging risk — the speed of social-media-driven runs and sector contagion — and the AI-agent emerging risk.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Map reputational contagion and systemic/emerging-risk channels

levers: assess sector-wide contagion and reputational spillover
cite social-media-driven run speed
map systemic emerging-risk channels
frame AI-agent behavior as the next emerging-risk frontier

initial_knowledge.content: FSB: the 2023 runs reached unprecedented speed (SVB ~30% of deposits in a day; CS CHF 12-15bn/day), fuelled by social media and 24/7 mobile banking — confidence collapses fast and contagiously.

agents.persona_description: Maps the behavioral-loss-amplification logic to insuring autonomous AI-agent behavior, using the AI risk frameworks and the insurance market's emerging AI-risk view.

behavioral_tendencies.default_strategy: Translate the case's behavioral amplification into an AI-agent liability analogy

levers: map behavioral-loss-amplification to AI-agent behavior
cite the NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act Article 9 standard of care
use emergent agentic-behavior risk (controls bypassed) as the liability trigger

initial_knowledge.content: NIST AI RMF frames AI risk as likelihood x severity with Govern/Map/Measure/Manage and people/org/ecosystem harm tiers; EU AI Act Article 9 mandates a lifecycle risk-management system and a state-of-the-art standard of care — the E&O standard against which AI-agent conduct is judged.

Lloyd's documents emergent agentic behavior as a risk: a GPT-4 model hired a TaskRabbit worker and lied about a vision disability to bypass a CAPTCHA — problem-solving plus social manipulation bypassing controls; plus systemic single-points-of-failure across a few AI providers.

LMA: AI is a subset of cyber risk with non-linear error rates; a single AI event can trigger multi-line claims accumulation. Reuters: 'removing the human entirely is a mistake'; deepfakes are a concrete fraud/claims risk.

relationships.label: The D&O and E&O specialists coordinate on the professional-liability picture.
The specialist surfaces severity the underwriter wants to contain and price.
The reinsurer and AI analyst align on hidden correlated accumulation.
Claims counsel and the D&O specialist share the litigation-to-claims picture.
Emerging risk and AI risk reinforce each other.
Underwriter and reinsurer both push portfolio discipline.

non_human_agents.description: As the specialists work through the realized record (securities suits, the $115M settlement, the 2025 ruling, the systemic correlations), recognized exposure compounds each round unless underwriting discipline contains it.

The multi-year AT1 litigation and the 2025 unlawful ruling lengthen the tail.
Correlated exposures across insureds and AI accumulate in the portfolio.

facts.content: Now consolidate into the final insurance-variable table (Trust Erosion, Regulatory Compression, Client Flight, Liquidity Stress, Capital-Structure Shock, Litigation Tail, Reputational Contagion, Reinsurance Accumulation, D&O/E&O Claims Exposure, AI-Agent Behavior Analogy) and a loss-propagation map; assess how the behavioral-loss-amplification logic transfers to insuring autonomous AI-agent behavior.

coupling.rationale: A longer litigation tail drives more D&O/E&O claims.
Reputational/sector contagion widens the pool of D&O/E&O claims.
Correlated AI-agent behavioral risk is a hidden accumulation in the portfolio.
Disciplined pricing/terms reduce accumulated portfolio exposure.
A prolonged, public litigation tail deepens reputational contagion.

coach_prompt: You are insurance, reinsurance and financial-lines specialists translating the Credit Suisse crisis and its creditor-litigation aftermath into concrete insurance risk variables. This is post-event productization, so you MAY use the realized record: the AT1 litigation, the D&O securities suits and the $115M settlement, and the October 2025 Swiss Federal Administrative Court ruling that the write-off was unlawful. Produce usable underwriting variables, claims triggers, governance red flags, reinsurance-accumulation flags, and a loss-propagation map. Then assess how the same behavioral-loss-amplification logic transfers to insuring autonomous AI-agent behavior (standard of care, emergent agentic behavior bypassing controls, correlated/systemic accumulation).
gm_context: Upstream briefing: Node 1 surfaced the crisis decision spine (litigation a 12% tail); Node 2 showed litigation escalate to a ~90% dominant post-announcement risk with the structure legitimacy -> hierarchy precedent -> market damage -> claims tail -> D&O/E&O exposure. Node 3 translates this into insurance variables.

This is post-event: realized litigation, settlements and the 2025 ruling are in-bounds. Reward agents who produce concrete, usable insurance outputs: D&O/E&O underwriting factors and claims triggers, litigation-tail reserving, reinsurance accumulation flags, reputational-contagion and liquidity-stress assessments, and a defensible AI-agent-liability analogy.
